`“Ageless Immortality.”
\

`If those words could be made absolutely true, they would offer one possible definition of eternity. Yet nothing in reality has ever attained such a state.\

`Even the vampires who surface now and again in legend cannot possess ageless immortality. They are defective things, unable to exist unless they plunder something from others. Worse, what replenishes them must come from their own kind—which, in most cases, means human beings. They possess no adaptability whatsoever. They may proclaim themselves a transcendent species, but theirs is not evolution. It is regression.
br
`Unless a species forms a perpetual motion machine unto itself, it cannot be called eternal. A life that depends upon others to remain ageless has no right to claim immortality.\

`Creatures already exist that approach perfection as self-sustaining perpetual motion machines. They consume themselves and reproduce from what they consume. They have no lifespan: old cells become nourishment, while new cells are born without end. Colonial organisms—jellyfish, for example. Yet such creatures function eternally only because they lack the superfluous faculty called intelligence. If intelligence may be discarded, that is no different from seeking eternity in death.\

`If one wishes to remain eternal while preserving human form, ageless immortality cannot provide the answer. The passage of ages will erode the body and wear all suppleness from the mind.\

`Immortality, or eternity. I have no attachment to that shopworn dream of deathlessness. So long as one clings to the individual, eternity is impossible.
br
`Rather than live forever as a single human being, I chose an infinity that would continue to exist for all eternity.\

;ブロック番号 120
*s120

bg "image\bg\ima_10.jpg",%type_nowaitdisp






`…If anyone would come into my room, it could only be Kohaku, Hisui, or Akiha.
`Hisui and Kohaku would both knock first, which leaves Akiha by elimination…
`“…Akiha?”
`I sit up in bed and call to her. The moonlight is weak, leaving the corners of the room drowned in shadow. I peer into them, but see no figure anywhere.\

`“…Maybe I imagined it.”
`Perhaps sleeplessness has put my nerves on edge. I let out a long breath and start to lie back down.

; 屋敷 : 部屋 : 志貴の部屋（夜）<瞬時表示>
bg "image\bg\bg_40c.jpg",%type_nowaitdisp


`The bedside lamp turns on by itself.
;S.E."心音"
wave se0

`“—Huh?”
`My heart jumps.
`“…That’s strange. I don’t remember touching the switch.”

; 屋敷 : 部屋 : 志貴の部屋（深夜）<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\bg_40d.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst


`I turn it off again. I have school tomorrow, and I really need to get some sleep.\

`“No, Brother. You’ll have to leave the light on.”
`A calm voice speaks suddenly from behind me.
`“—!”
`I spin around, and there—

; 秋葉 : 01～10 : 04_楽04（微笑・私服）<左シャッター(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\aki_t04b.jpg",%type_lshutter_fst

`… ………… ……………………

`“Morn…ing.” My foggy mind surfaced into wakefulness. Sunlight streamed through the window, filling the room with a drowsy warmth.
br
`“……”
br
`I stared at my hands. Their palms were faintly damp, and sweat covered my whole body as if I had spent the night in sweltering heat. My breath was coming rough and ragged, too.\

`“Ah…” I flexed both hands gingerly. “…They work…” There were no rope marks on my wrists. The bed was clean; the chair Akiha had occupied was gone, and so was Kohaku.\

`“Huh…?”
br
`Akiha and Kohaku…?
br
`“K-Kohaku?” I shot upright like a spring-loaded doll and swept my eyes around the room. But there was— “No one… here…” No one at all. The bed showed no sign of disturbance, and there was certainly no devilish little Kohaku waiting beside it.\

`“A dream…” The moment I understood, a breath of relief escaped me. I closed my eyes and forced my breathing back into rhythm. This was my room. It was not yet seven in the morning. I was alone, and of course neither Kohaku nor Akiha was here. “Haaaaah…” I knew that. I knew it had been a dream. Once I thought clearly, there was no possibility that Akiha and the others would ever come and do something like that. The events of last night fell apart at that one simple fact.\

`“Haaaaah…” I emptied my lungs of the breath trapped inside them. …Even so, the scenes from last night remained vivid in my mind. I knew they were a dream, but every sensation had been so real that they still felt like something that had truly happened. …Nevertheless, it had unquestionably been a dream. That was the only scrap of comfort I had.\

`“But why…?” Why would I dream something like that? …Yes, Kohaku was cute. She was the one person in this mansion I found easiest to relax around, and simply seeing her cheerful face could lift my own spirits. But that didn’t make what happened in the dream right. Kohaku was practically family to me. I had never thought of her as—a woman.\

`“Ugh…” And yet Kohaku’s teasing eyes came straight back to me. “Damn it. What the hell am I thinking?” I shook my head, trying to fling the dream out of it. And then—

`“Why…?”

`“Urk…”
`I remembered Akiha’s gaze, cold as ice, and clutched my own arm to reassure myself that this was reality.\

`“Damn it—what am I thinking?!”
`Lusting after my own sister meant something was seriously wrong with me. True, after eight years apart, Akiha seemed like a completely different person—more an unfamiliar young lady than my sister.
`“But… she was… cute…”

`The sports clubs were holding their morning practices on the field. I wasn’t in any club now, but I did enjoy being active. My coordination was good enough that I could take a little pride in it.
br
`But joining a club had never been possible. Chronic anemia meant I might let everyone down when they needed me most, and my doctor had strictly forbidden me from exercising too often.\

`Ever since middle school, I had been invited to join clubs more times than I could count. Every time, I turned them down with the same line: “It’s not really me.” And every time I did, I felt some nameless gulf open between us. Perhaps it had always been a wall buried deep inside me—the knowledge that, no matter what I did, I could never truly join the people on the other side.\

`“……” Oh, enough. Brooding like this wasn’t me either. I cut the pointless sentimentality short and headed for the classroom.\

`Fourth period is Contemporary Society. With lunch so close, the whole classroom has grown restless.
br
`It is Wednesday, so we have one fewer lesson than usual. After lunch comes homeroom, when we are supposedly spending an hour choosing our class project for the cultural festival. Better still, tomorrow is the school’s founding anniversary, which means a day off. Once fourth period ends, the holiday has effectively begun. No wonder everyone is waiting so eagerly for the bell.\

`“—So sleepy.” I smother a yawn. The lesson passes without incident, and the day continues without the slightest irregularity.
br
`Come to think of it, perhaps I am the strange one for sitting through class so peacefully after everything abnormal I have experienced. Once school ends and night falls, I will be working with Arcueid again. If I think about what that means, I probably have no business taking it this easy.\

`I study my reflection in the window. For some reason, Shiki Tohno is smiling as if he is enjoying himself. “—Hmph.” I sternly tighten my mouth. It cannot be that I enjoy roaming the streets at night with Arcueid. So what exactly am I so excited about?

I, too, regret that matters ended this way.” The enemy twisted his mouth into a chuckle.\

`When I came to, I was lying in a hospital bed. The curtains swayed back and forth. Outside, the sky was beautifully clear, and a dry wind announced the end of summer.\

`“Pleased to meet you, Shiki Tohno. Congratulations on your recovery.”
br
`The man I had never seen before said this and offered me his hand. His cheerful smile and square glasses suited him perfectly. So did his spotless white coat.\

`“Shiki, do you understand what I’m saying?” “No… Why am I in a hospital?” “You don’t remember. You were caught in a traffic accident while you were walking down the street. A shard of glass went into your chest. It wasn’t the sort of wound anyone should have survived.” Still smiling, the man in white said something that didn’t sound like a doctor at all.\
br
br
br
br
br
br
`――――――I felt horribly, horribly sick.\

`“I’m sleepy. Can I go to sleep?” “Of course. Don’t strain yourself. For now, you should concentrate on getting well.” The doctor kept smiling. I could hardly stand to look at him. “Doctor, can I ask you something?” “What is it, Shiki?” “Why do you have scribbles all over your body? This room is full of cracks too. It looks like it might fall apart any second.”
br
`For the briefest instant, the doctor’s smile slipped. Then it returned, as cheerful as ever, and he strode away with his heels clicking.\

`“There does seem to be something wrong with his brain. Call Dr. Ashiya in neurosurgery. His eyes may be damaged as well; schedule an examination for this afternoon.”
br
`The doctor whispered this to a nurse so that I wouldn’t hear.\

`“How strange… Everyone’s covered in scribbles.” Black, tangled lines ran through the whole hospital. When I touched one, my fingertip sank softly into it. “Oh.” I thought something thinner might sink even deeper, so I took the fruit knife from the bedside cabinet and traced the scribble with it.\

`Without the slightest pressure, the knife sank into the bed all the way to the hilt. It was fun, so I drew the blade along the rest of the scribble.
br
`Thud.
br
`The bed came apart in two clean halves with a heavy crash. “Aaaaaah!”
br
`The girl in the next bed screamed. The nurses came running and took the fruit knife away from me.\

`Whenever I cut along one of those scribbles, whatever it was came apart cleanly. I didn’t need any strength. It was as easy as cutting paper with scissors. Beds. Chairs. Desks. Walls. Floors.
br
`…I never tried it, but probably—surely—people too.\

`Apparently, no one else could see the scribbles. For some reason, the black lines were visible only to me. Even though I was a child, I slowly began to understand what they were. They had to be seams: weak places, like the skin where an operation had been stitched closed. Otherwise, there was no way a child like me could cut through a wall.
br
`――――Oh. I never knew.
br
`That the whole world was made of seams, and was such a terribly breakable place.\

`No one else could see them, so no one else was afraid. But I could. I was too frightened to walk. It felt as though I were the only person who had gone wrong.\

`Maybe that was why. Two weeks had passed, and still no one believed me. Two weeks had passed, and still no one had come to see me.
br
`Two whole weeks—and all that time, I alone had been living in a world made of seams…\

`After that, going to the field each afternoon became part of my day. The woman got angry if I called her Aoko. She said she hated her name. After thinking hard, I decided to call her Teach, since she always acted as though she knew best.\

`Teach listened seriously to everything and could settle any worry of mine with a single sentence. The accident had left me gloomy, but thanks to her I slowly became myself again. Even the scribbles that had frightened me so badly seemed less frightening when I talked to her. I had no idea who she really was, but perhaps she truly was a schoolteacher after all.
br
`But I didn’t think any of that mattered. Being with Teach made me happy. Surely that simple truth was the important part.\

`The next day—exactly seven days after we had met—Teach came to the field carrying a large suitcase in one hand.\

`“Here. Wear these and you won’t see those strange scribbles anymore.” Teach had brought me a pair of glasses. “But my eyes aren’t bad.” “Just put them on. There’s no prescription in them.” She forced the glasses onto my face. And then—\

`“Wow! This is amazing, Teach! I can’t see any scribbles at all!” “Of course not. I stole the eye-blocking lenses from my sister’s place to make those—a masterpiece bearing the full force of Aoko Aozaki’s genius. If you treat them carelessly, you’ll answer to me, Shiki.” “I’ll take good care of them! But you really are incredible, Teach. All those horrible lines are gone. It’s like magic!”
br
`“Naturally. I’m a Magician, after all.”
br
`Teach grinned with immense satisfaction and set the suitcase on the ground.\

`“But listen, Shiki. The lines haven’t disappeared. The glasses only hide them. Take the glasses off, and you’ll see them again.” “R-really?” “Yes. There is no curing this. You’ll have to find a way to live with those eyes.” “…I don’t want them. I don’t want such frightening eyes. What if I cut another line and break my promise to you?” “Oh, that promise never to trace another line? Don’t be silly. You can break a promise like that whenever you like.” “…I can? But you said it was a terrible thing to do.”\

`“It is wrong. But that power belongs to you alone, Shiki. Whether you use it is your choice, and no one else has the right to condemn you. You may have those Mystic Eyes of Death Perception precisely because a day lies in your future when you’ll need them. I can’t ask you to deny all that you are.” Teach crouched until her eyes were level with mine.\

`“I’m not asking you to become a saint. Grow into the kind of adult you believe is right. A boy who can accept that he has done wrong and honestly say he is sorry will surely become a fine young man in ten years.”

`“Oh, but don’t take those glasses off unless the situation is truly desperate. Unusual powers draw other unusual powers. br
`Teach turned her back on me.\

`“This is goodbye, then. Shiki, everyone’s life is full of pitfalls. You have more power to deal with them than most people, so stand up straight.” Teach began to walk away. I was terribly sad, but I was her friend, so I stood tall and saw her off.\

`“All right. Goodbye, Teach.” “Good. That was very well done, Shiki. Keep that spirit and stay well. Remember: when trouble comes, calm yourself first, then think everything through. Don’t worry. You’ll manage perfectly well on your own.” Teach smiled, and she looked happy.\

`My body is once again lying well away from her. A faint odor of gunpowder clings to my shoulder.
br
`“Ah… ah… ah.” When the gun-blade entered me, she pulled the trigger. The blast threw me away and opened the distance between us again.\

; 中央<夜>=シエル:睨み01（睨んでます・完全武装）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\cel_t06c.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“Twice in succession cannot be chance. If even that much blood loss has not killed you through shock, does that mean your body has begun to change?”
br
`The weapon clacks, replacing the blade at its tip with a fresh one. The sword that shot me drops to the ground, then flutters apart into pages torn from a book.\

`“That’s… that’s impossible.” Yet the impossible thing terrifies me. Merely touching my body, that weapon delivers a fatal poison. Death. I will die. There is no doubt—she will kill me.\

; 白画面<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_11b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
; 学校校庭（夜）<クロスフェード(速)>

`Am I going to die? Is that what frightens me? I don’t know.
br
`“Ah… ngh…!”
br
`My shoulder is on fire. The heat is so fierce it feels ready to consume my entire body.\

`With a metallic click, Ciel resets the weapon. Twice. Surviving it twice was nothing short of a miracle. The next strike will surely—\

; 白画面<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_11b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
; 学校校庭（夜）<クロスフェード(速)>

;S.E."心音・速(ループ)"
waveloop se1


`I imagine that gun-blade burying itself in the center of my face and gouging onward. The image is not so much frightening as hideous.
br
`Death—whatever shape it takes—is ugly, filthy, and revolting. I like myself. That is why I do not want that to happen to me.\

`Is that why I’m afraid? I don’t know. Now that I think of it, for all the “death” I have seen, I have never once truly thought about what death is.\

`No. None of that matters now. “Hah, hah, hah—” I have to run. If I do not want to die, then right now I have to run.

br
; 中央<夜>=シエル:睨み01（睨んでます・完全武装）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\cel_t07c.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“Aren’t you going to take off your glasses?” Her voice is flat and artificial. The meaning of those words hits me all at once. Taking off my glasses means seeing the “lines” on her body. If I do that, I might kill her—\

`“Wh-what are you saying, Ciel…?!”
; 中央<夜>=シエル:睨み01（睨んでます・完全武装）<クロスフェード(速)>

`“You… damn thing…!” Perhaps pain has lost all meaning, because I wrench the sword free. It has passed clean through me, so in sheer anger I pull it the rest of the way out through my chest. “Good…!” Now I can escape into the building.\


`“What do you think running will accomplish, Tohno?”
br
`Before I can move, her voice comes from behind me.\

`“Do you still not understand? How fast do you imagine you ran from the schoolyard to here? Why are wounds that should be fatal failing to kill you?”\

`“No—” My mind washes white. Don’t be fooled. Don’t be fooled. That woman has deceived you all along. Never listen to her again. If you listen, you will die. Ignore her. Reject her. Even if she speaks the truth, this body has no choice now but to cast it aside—\

`“Stop… it.” “There is nowhere left to run. Your only choices are to fight or be killed. If you cannot fight, then death is all that remains.” Click, click. Her footsteps draw closer.\

`“—!” My body springs. My back, shoulder, and arm are nearly dead, yet my body launches itself as if those wounds were trivial.
br
`―――I can hardly believe it myself. Breathing raggedly, I race into the school at a speed that rivals hers.\

`“Hah, hah, hah, hah—” I run. Thinking of nothing, wanting only to escape from something, I keep running.\

`“Hah, hah, hah, hah—” At last I reach my limit. Perhaps I have simply run out of breath; perhaps my wounds are so grave my limbs have ceased to work. There is little difference now.\

`“Hah… hah… hah—” I reach the end of the corridor. The blank wall leaves me nowhere else to go, and I collapse. Flat on my back, I strain to rise—then realize how ridiculous that is.\

`“…Hah… hah… hah.” I sit half cross-legged on the floor and let my back rest against the wall. Knees raised, head thrown back, I draw a deep breath.\

`“The moon…” Moonlight shows through the window above me. Perhaps exhaustion is to blame, but everything I see looks hollow, as if veiled in mist.
br
`Hollow. Does that mean uncertain? Like me. Like the human being called Shiki Tohno—uncertain.\

`“…Hur…ts…” Pain throbs through my shoulder. If I had been as certain as this pain, would any of this have happened?\

`I no longer know. All my life I believed I was Shiki Tohno. But apparently that person exists elsewhere, while I am an adopted child of unknown origin. If I was adopted into the Tohno house, I ought to remember the life I led before it—yet I remember nothing at all. Truly, the only memories I possess belong to Shiki Tohno.\

; 黒画面<クロスフェード(速)>

`A solitary moon hangs in the night sky. “…” How strange. How did I never notice before? Tonight is so—\

; 学校廊下2（夜）<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\bg_11c.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

br
`…In the end, what was I? I know nothing about myself, and now even that self is about to disappear. It’s absurd.
br
`Everything is blurred and vague. Absurd. A world where death is visible. A field of vision in which death can be perceived. That day eight years ago, I met the woman who taught me how to live, and because of her I managed to live a decent life. Even now, I can say without hesitation that meeting her was right.\

`“But… it looks like I was never someone who should have been allowed to live.” Perhaps I ought to take my own life while enough of me remains to think so. But I cannot. I cannot kill myself. However ugly it was, however wrong, I wanted to live.\

`If I die, everything becomes a lie. I want to live. No matter how wrong I am, no matter how much I lose, I want to live.
br
`If only she were here. If only Ciel had stayed with me, I would not have cared what else I lost.\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――For that alone, I kept myself alive. But now even that is over. Five years. I cannot really say whether they were long or short.\

`“…Liar.” I never wanted to hear those words.\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――I am grateful to you, Tohno. My work is finished now. All that remains is to discharge the responsibility I still bear.\

`“…You liar.” Yet perhaps there had been truth as well. She deceived me, yes—but not even once had she ever—\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――Thank you for everything. I cannot remember the last time I was this happy. So let us shake hands one final time.\

`“…God, you liar.” Not once. Not once had she actually lied to me.\

br
br
br
br
br
`―――After I am gone, please stay friends with Inui. I wanted to be a student like you and him—\

`“…” But her very existence had been the lie. Even so, I cannot believe that smile was false.\

`But this is what reality amounts to. Ciel was a lie. She stayed beside me only so that she could kill me. I had been deceived. She had never loved me. Helping me when I was falling apart, wasting our breaks together for no reason—every moment of it was only meant to determine whether I was Roa.\

`My teeth grind. I clamp my jaw until my molars ache.
br
`“…Damn it.” Bitter with frustration, I claw at the wall. Yes. I had been deceived. Every step Ciel took toward me was calculated.\

`“…And yet…” My fingertips brush the wall, aching with a grief I cannot name. Yes, she deceived me. But even so—
br
`“I can’t hate her.”
!w1000

\

`I could never hate her. Even if it was a lie to her, I was happy. Nothing can make that untrue. I knew her for less than two weeks, and yet I had been so—so genuinely happy.
br
`“…Damn it—” That is why I cannot hate her. Yet that illusion belonged to me alone. That alone is what makes it so bitter.\

`My vision blurs. Beyond the window lies a white night. The silent school seems sunk at the bottom of the sea, wavering gently around me.
br
`Everything is false, a vision that vanishes when approached. One vast mirage, forever beyond my grasp.

`I talk with the man for roughly an hour. We watch the passing cars and discuss one meaningless subject after another. `“No. I can’t kill something so vague that it can only exist as a figure of speech.” “Bullshit. To kill sight, you destroy the eyes. To kill hearing, you destroy the ears. Even I could do that. Wherever I went, I felt as though my family and I would always be strangers.”

`“—Why? I’m not really your brother.” “…Honestly. After everything I’ve said, you still don’t understand. You are the only person I could ever call my brother. Even if you can’t accept that, I still want you beside me. Because I love you, Brother.”\

`“Wha—” Akiha says something astonishing as casually as if it were nothing. I’m happy that she cares for me as her brother. Yet the more she does—the more impossible it becomes for me to remain in this mansion.\

`“…No. I’m not the person you think I am. You call SHIKI a murderer, but I might be one too—someone no different from him.” “A murderer? What do you mean?” “…”
br
`After coming this far, I can’t keep hiding it. I tell her everything that has happened—the dream of murder last night, the bloodstains I couldn’t remember leaving, and the dream in which Akiha killed me.\

`“…I can’t trust myself. No matter what I tell myself, I can’t believe that was only a dream. Father wrote that the Nanaya family produced killers. So one day I’ll become like SHIKI and bring you nothing but misery.” I wrench the confession from the depths of my heart. Yet Akiha only widens her eyes, then struggles to suppress an amused laugh.\

`“W-what’s so funny? This isn’t a joke. …You may not believe me, but I really dreamed that I drank someone’s blood…!” Akiha is still laughing softly. …Somehow, it makes all the hours I spent suffering alone feel ridiculous.\

`“Oh, it is funny. Listen to me, Brother. You are not a vampire. The Nanaya blood is exceptional, but entirely human. And the Nanayas are not killers. …Father might have seen them that way, certainly, but the Nanayas feel a murderous impulse only toward things that look human yet are not. So what you saw was nothing more than a dream. Even that dream was only a residue of thought that leaked into you from the killer called SHIKI. It reflects none of your own desires.”\

`…Thoughts leaking from SHIKI? Now that she mentions it, Father’s journal did say something like that. SHIKI stole my life and joined it to his through coalescence, so the two of us affect each other—or something along those lines.\

`“…I see. But then who is killing people in the city? Even if what I’m seeing is a dream, there are real victims out there—”
br
`―――The killer exists. I feel as though I have met him before. Did that happen in a dream too? No, whether it did or not, if a killer is loose in this city, then he must be—\

`“…SHIKI is still alive…?” “What?” Even Akiha, who had been hiding her laughter until now, turns grave.\

`“Akiha, Father’s journal said SHIKI survived. That means—” “Father’s journal…?” Akiha tilts her head in genuine puzzlement. “Father wrote that SHIKI and I were connected. Then the dreams I’m seeing may be SHIKI’s.” …No. More likely, they are the murders SHIKI himself is committing.\

`“…That is possible. Father’s death was suspicious in several respects, and there were signs that someone had been hidden in the cells beneath the mansion.” “…Wait, Akiha. There are underground cells in this house?” “Why, of course. Many members of the Tohno family suffer mental disturbances. We need such facilities to prevent them from harming the outside world. Though that isn’t their only use. Father often locked me there when I disobeyed him as a child.” For some reason, Akiha gives me a sidelong look of delight. …A chill runs down my back.\

`“…Fine. Forget the cells. We need to do something about SHIKI. If he really is murdering people in the city, we have to stop him.” “Do we? Whatever SHIKI has become, why should we involve ourselves? The police exist for precisely this reason. Wouldn’t it be better to leave murderers to them?”\

`“What—Akiha, how can you say that? Murderer or not, SHIKI is still your brother. He has to answer for his crimes, but even so—” “…Good grief. How can you possibly be this kindhearted, Brother?” With an exasperated sigh, Akiha sweeps back her hair.\

`“You are my only family, Brother. SHIKI means nothing to me, and you have no reason to grieve over him.” “Idiot, we can’t just ignore this. He’s evaded the police until now—what makes you think they’ll suddenly catch him? What if he claims another victim in the meantime?” “Then he does. That would not be our responsibility.” Akiha says it while staring directly into my eyes.\

`“Can’t we stop talking about this? Murder and killers make for such tedious conversation.” “Wha—” I try to say this concerns our own family, but the words won’t come. …Akiha’s eyes are fathomless, as though they can see through to the center of my heart. Under that gaze, I feel inexplicably incapable of opposing her, and my resolve drains away.\

`“I see you understand. Would you return to your room now? I’ve only just come home from school, and I have things to do.” “…” …For the moment, Akiha is right: there is nothing more to say. Still unconvinced, I nod and turn my back on her.\

bg "image\bg\ima_10.jpg",%type_lcartain_mid

; 屋敷外周<左カーテン(中)>

`I reached the source of the noise. “……Huh?”
br
`Awooooooooooo.
br
`The howling had not stopped. Yet there was not a dog in sight. There was only—a human figure. A man in a black coat stood alone beneath a streetlamp, its island of light cut from the darkness.
br
`The howling came from beside the man.
`―――――Yet there was no dog anywhere.\

; 白画面<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_11b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
; 屋敷外周<左カーテン(中)>

`The man in the coat was extremely tall. Broad and powerfully built, he stood motionless with his back to me.\

`“……”
br
`My throat dries. The dog’s drawn-out howl pounds against my eardrums. The night air clings damply to my skin.
br
`Nothing has happened. Nothing at all. Yet breathing and moving feel unbearably heavy, as though I were trapped at the bottom of the sea—\

`Kwaa.
br
`The sound came from above. With a sudden flap of wings, the deep-blue crow descended onto the man’s shoulder.
br
`―――And then—
br
`The crow abruptly vanished.\

`“……What?” Had my eyes deceived me? It looked as though the crow had disappeared inside the black coat.
br
`“……”
br
`The black coat turns.
; 中央<夜>=ネロ:ギョロ目<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\nero_t03.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`Beneath the white streetlamp, the figure was quite literally a shadow.\

`A mass of black. Within it, only the eyes shone—eyes filled with a cold intelligence as keen and lethal as a weapon—
br
`“……Ah.”
br
`I cannot breathe. Fortunately—his eyes seem not to see me at all.\
br
br
br
br
br
br
br
`“Not here, then.”\
br
; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(中)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_mid

`The black coat walks away.\

`Only after the figure had vanished completely could I breathe again. “Hah—haa… ah.” Relief emptied my lungs.
br
`Only then did I realize that the dogs had stopped howling.\

; 黒画面<クロスフェード(遅)>
bg "image\bg\ima_10.jpg",%type_crossfade_slw
; 志貴の部屋（深夜）<左カーテン(遅)>

`I returned to my room. There was no sign that Akiha or the others had awakened. Apparently I was the only one who had found the howling unbearable.
br
`“Ngh—”
br
`What was wrong with me? My head still hurt.\

`“Why… why am I shaking?” My fingers were trembling. My whole body shuddered in tiny spasms, and an unnatural cold ran down my back.
br
`If I had to put it into words—
br
`It felt as though someone had torn out my spinal cord and driven a pillar of ice into its place.\


; 白画面<クロスフェード(速)>
bg "image\bg\ima_11b.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
; 志貴の部屋（深夜）<左カーテン(遅)>
bg "image\bg\bg_40c.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“……” The room lurched. Was it my usual anemia? I felt my consciousness plummeting toward the floor.
br
`And on the way down, I saw something horrible.\

; 志貴の部屋（死の線）<左シャッター(遅)>
bg "image\bg\bg_40f.jpg",%type_lshutter_mid

`“What—” I could see those “lines” despite my glasses. “Ugh……” Perhaps because I had not seen them at all lately, the backlash was worse. Nausea rose in me. Combined with the dizziness, it left me on the verge of vomiting.\

`“……What the hell is happening?” I couldn’t understand. As long as my eyes remained open, those hideous scribbles forced themselves into my vision.
br
`―――A nightmare. That was all.
br
`Somehow I collapsed onto the bed. ……Yes. I only had to sleep. The quickest way to deny what I was seeing was to stop seeing anything at all.\

`My body would barely move. I could lie here like a corpse, sprawled across the bed, and sink into sleep as deep and heavy as mud—\

Their howling had long since stopped. The mansion was so quiet that the clock’s second hand echoed through the night.\

`“……?” There it was again. Somewhere inside the house—perhaps the foyer. “……A burglar?” It was not impossible. This absurd mansion seemed to be constructed entirely out of valuables, and at present only Akiha, Kohaku, Hisui, and I were living here. “……” I slipped out of bed and left the room without making a sound.\

`“……!” No—someone was there. A figure had entered through the front door and was staggering unsteadily across the foyer—

`“……What was she doing out this late?” The empty foyer offered no answer. After watching for a while longer, I returned quietly to my room.\

`――――I dreamed an old, familiar dream.
br
`It was the end of summer, eight years ago. After my terrible injury, after they transferred me to a hospital where no one came to visit, after I met my teacher. When I returned to the estate, Father told me I was being sent to live with a family I had never met.
br
`It all happened with startling abruptness. The day after I left the hospital, I was sent to the Arima house.\

`I remember the sky was blue and utterly cloudless. Autumn was just beginning. Someone took my hand and led me away from the Tohno estate.
br
`But shortly before I left, that girl slipped past the adults and came to see me.\

; 志貴過去回想1（夏の日差し）<クロスフェード(中)>
bg "image\bg\cmo_20.jpg",%type_crossfade_mid


br
br
br
br
br
br
`“When it’s time for you to leave, come to the tree in the back garden.” She told me that, so I escaped Father’s notice and went there.\

`The blue sky. Beneath a blue sky that seemed deep enough to fall into forever, she waited alone. As far as I knew, it was the first time she had ever ventured outside the mansion.\

`“Take this with you.” The girl untied the ribbon from her hair and placed it in my hand. It must have been a farewell gift, but I was only a child and did not feel particularly pleased.
br
`……After all, I doubt any nine-year-old boy would be delighted to receive a ribbon.\

`“That ribbon is my favorite. So make sure you return it to me later.” Those words saved me.
br
`Return it to me, the girl said. Return to me, I heard.
br
`――――That alone was enough. On the last day, when not one person came to see me off, I was glad she had said it—even though we had never spoken before.\

`―――But I could not tell her, “I’ll be sure to return it.”
br
`At the one time I wished I could have been foolish, I must have understood that I would never be allowed to return to this house.
br
`……That was all we said. The girl’s eyes were cold as ice, yet there was something sad in them. When the time came, I walked back toward the entrance. She remained where she was, standing like a doll and watching me go.\

br
br
br
br
br
br
`blue sky. not one cloud. a faraway dream of one bright day.\

As long as we live, every one of us will make mistakes. …It is sad, but unavoidable. To live is to be worn away. We are creatures whose very passage through the world changes something else as we ourselves are diminished.”\

`“…That doesn't help. If everyone does wrong, there's no salvation in it. I don't like examples like that.” “…You're right. That alone offers no salvation. But a sin can be atoned for, can't it? The world contains only those who can atone and those who cannot. So I think the truly lost are those who, no matter what they do, cannot atone for their own sins.”
br
`…For some reason, her voice sounded terribly sad.\

`“But you are someone who can atone, Tohno. I don’t know what mistake you made, but I know that much. If worry is keeping you awake, think about how you will live and atone from now on. It’s such a difficult problem that sooner or later your brain will give out, and then you’ll fall asleep for certain.” Her words were so full of jokes that I couldn’t tell how much she meant.\

`“…Someone who can atone. But my mistake can’t ever be made right. That much I know.” “Of course. No sin can ever truly be undone. If you hurt someone and later heal the wound, the fact that you hurt them does not disappear. However hard you try, the wrong you committed will never cease to have happened.\
`Atonement, I think, is not an outcome but a process. That is what separates those who can atone from those who cannot. And you, Tohno, are unquestionably someone who can.”\

`“…I don’t understand. I’m a terrible person. I’m not nearly as good as you think.” “That’s easy enough to see. Earlier, I was actually rather moved. You have an enormous scar on your chest, don’t you?” “Yes… but what about it?” “A scar like that must have come from a terrible accident. …Such wounds leave marks on the heart as well. One that large, one that still hasn’t faded, is hardly ordinary.\

`“Yet you’re perfectly ordinary. The strength it took for someone with a scar like that to go on living a normal life is unquestionably something to be proud of. You must have had a very honest, wholesome childhood.” After murmuring that with satisfaction, she fell silent. When I listened closely, I could hear her slow, peaceful breathing. “…Did you fall asleep?” There was no answer. Only the steady sound of rain beyond the room.\

`“…Atonement.” A punishment equal to the crime. Would the body of the woman I had killed be discovered tomorrow and reported as the latest grotesque murder? When that happened, the things I would lose were beyond counting. I would bring disgrace and trouble to Akiha, and I would never again be able to talk with Ciel like this. “…”\

`But if accepting all that could become atonement, then I had no choice but to accept it. If it could atone for what I had done, then perhaps something resembling salvation did exist somewhere. “Haaah…” I was beginning to feel sleepy. I didn’t know what tomorrow would bring. But if I was allowed even this much, I wanted to go on living this life until the moment my crime was discovered and I was called to answer for it.\

; 屋外一般 : 公園・路地裏 : 公園Ｂ（死の線あり）<瞬時表示>
bg "image\bg\bg_29c.jpg",%type_nowaitdisp

`…No. It’s too soon. Nrvnqsr has only just arrived. I need him to focus on Arcueid a little longer, or I will never manage a surprise attack.\

; 左<夜>=アルクェイド:睨み03（02のさらにキツイ感じ）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t07.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“Don’t be mistaken, Nrvnqsr. There aren’t twenty-seven Dead Apostle Ancestors left in the world, but twenty-eight. Do none of you acknowledge the Serpent as one of your own?”

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst

; 右<夜>=ネロ:通常<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\nero_t02a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“Of course not. His ideals differ fundamentally from ours. He belongs to the vampiric species, yet his existence as such has no meaning. Most Dead Apostles therefore refuse to recognize him as a compatriot.”\

; 右<夜>=ネロ:通常<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\nero_t02c.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“—That said, he and I are old acquaintances. I flatter myself that I understand him more deeply than the other Dead Apostles do.”

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst

; 左<夜>=アルクェイド:睨み03（02のさらにキツイ感じ）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t07.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“…I see. Come to think of it, you differ from the other vampiric species just as the Serpent does. Perhaps heretics share common tastes.”\

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst


; 右<夜>=ネロ:通常<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\nero_t02a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst
`“Quite the contrary. A heretic is a heretic precisely because he stands alone. Exile from the herd gives two outcasts no cause to understand one another.”

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst
; 左<夜>=アルクェイド:睨み03（02のさらにキツイ感じ）<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\ark_t07.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Is that so? You both pursued me all the way to this country. That seems rather similar to me.”

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst
; 右<夜>=ネロ:通常<クロスフェード(速)>
ld c,":a;image\tachi\nero_t02a.jpg",%type_crossfade_fst

`“Enough. By that measure, your own caprice is far more extravagant. You exist to execute the surviving Dead Apostles, so why pursue the Serpent of Akasha with such tenacity? The Serpent cannot be venom potent enough to merit the obsession of the Princess of the True Ancestors.”\

; 中央を消去<クロスフェード(速)>
cl c,%type_crossfade_fst

`Nrvnqsr’s voice rises ever so slightly. Arcueid’s taunts must be working: he has eyes only for the white woman who is his enemy.
br
`―――What do I do?
br
